_meta.what: Rules the line learned from its own runs, one entry each: the rule in plain words, the failure it came from, and (where a machine can check it) the name of the check that is run over every new brief before a council member sees it.
_meta.how_it_grows: A RED run drafts one lesson; a council member accepts it with a passkey and it is appended here. Earlier lessons are never reworded or dropped. `fired` lists where a lesson later changed or refused a brief.

lessons.rule: A brief names its product by the product's recorded id, exactly as recorded. It is never re-spelled, re-cased or guessed; the line resolves the repository from that id itself.
lessons.failure: The first Upread ticket spelled the product's repository 'upread' where the record says 'Upread'. One letter of case: the line would have refused the run at its first step, before any building.

lessons.rule: A ticket is one feature. A ticket that lists several deliverables says what is out of scope and leaves it to a later ticket; one large ticket ends as a 45-minute timeout, not a product.
lessons.failure: One ticket asked for the reader, PDF reading, link extraction and tests together. RED after 2701 s with no build script written; 5 of 6 checks failed. The next ticket (reader only, PDFs named as out of scope) went GREEN in 455 s.

lessons.rule: The builder writes project files early and improves them; a run that plans and inspects first runs out of time with nothing to check. Every ticket's task says so.
lessons.failure: The RED run made 22 model calls and 18 shell commands in 2701 s and wrote no project file before the 2700 s limit. The GREEN ticket's task opened with "write files early".

fired.what: task ends with "Write files early; do not audit dependency source."
task ends with "Write files early; do not audit dependency source."

lessons.rule: The builder does not read or audit the source of installed libraries: their versions, licences and bundled URLs are not its job. Every ticket's task says so.
lessons.failure: Commands 3 to 18 of the RED run looked through an installed PDF library for web addresses in its bundled files. None of them built the app.

fired.what: covered by the same closing line, "Write files early; do not audit dependency source."
covered by the same closing line, "Write files early; do not audit dependency source."

lessons.rule: No check that cannot pass. A no_external_hosts check cannot pass on a build that bundles a library, because bundled code carries URLs; a ticket that installs dependencies does not carry one and proves the same thing with a file check on the built page.
lessons.failure: The RED ticket carried both `npm ci` and a no_external_hosts check on dist. The builder spent its run searching a library for 'http' instead of building, and the check failed anyway because dist was never built. The GREEN ticket left the check out.

lessons.rule: A product is created by an approved brief, never by a chat command. When asked in chat to create or launch a product, say that a brief has to be drafted and approved by the council first.
lessons.failure: A conversation asked for Upread by its id before any brief had been approved and was refused: no such product. Upread existed as a product only once its brief was approved, about 90 minutes later.

lessons.rule: A brief's title and task carry no budget figures or money words. The budget has its own field; the title and the task are what the public brief card shows.
lessons.failure: Upread's announcement text repeated the ticket's $15 budget and was held back before anyone outside the council saw it.

lessons.rule: After a RED run, write a smaller ticket, not a retry of the same one: cut the task to the part the run reached, name the rest as out of scope, lower the budget. The same task sent again fails the same way.
lessons.failure: The all-in-one ticket ($15 budget) went RED after 2701 s having spent $3.98. The smaller ticket that followed (1 of 2, $8 budget) went GREEN on its first attempt in 455 s for $0.62.
